title: Static Map URL Helper: Map Images by Address Bar
description: Build static map image URLs with the Static Map URL Helper — centre, zoom, size and markers as URL parameters, for documents and email. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a 640-pixel-wide static map at zoom 15 in New York spans about 2.3 kilometres — wide enough for a neighbourhood, tight enough to read street names.
quick_answer: The Static Map URL Helper builds static map image URLs — a map picture whose centre, zoom, size and markers are all written into the URL itself. Set the view and copy the address: the map arrives as an image — no JavaScript required.

body.t: Reports, invoices and property packs need maps that print. A static image behaves like any picture in a document — the interactive helpers (
Mail clients block scripts and iframes; images survive. A static map is the only map an email can carry reliably.
Slides want a fixed view that will not pan mid-talk. The static URL freezes exactly the framing you rehearsed.
Listing cards and link previews use map images as pictures — small sizes at moderate zooms, generated by URL on the fly.

The URL is the map's recipe: centre coordinates, a zoom, pixel dimensions, a marker at the centre. Change the zoom number and the same URL serves a wider world — the recipe is legible, which is why debugging it is easy.

At zoom 15 in New York one pixel covers 3.62 m, so a 640-px image spans ~2.32 km. Want the whole borough? Raise the size or drop the zoom — the arithmetic is the metres-per-pixel family's, applied to a picture.

faq: Which providers' URL shapes are covered?

The helper builds the common static-map URL patterns (the OpenStreetMap-based static services and the familiar parameter styles). Each provider's own terms, attribution and key rules apply to the images served.
Open map data requires visible attribution wherever the image is used — keep the credit line with the picture, in documents as on the web.
How large can the image be?
Providers cap dimensions (common flavours cap near 640–1280 px per side, retina modes doubling pixels). For print, request the largest the service allows and place it at a size its pixels can honour.
Can the image show a route or area?
Some static services accept path and polygon parameters — the URL grows long and fragile. For complex overlays, an interactive embed ages better.
Why does my image look stale?
Static tiles cache; satellite and map vintages differ by area. The URL fetches the provider's current render, whose date is the provider's, not yours.
Tile and static servers are shared infrastructure with usage policies. For heavy or commercial traffic, fetch politely, cache locally where terms allow, or use a paid tier.
Addresses resolve to coordinates first — geocode the place, then build the URL around the pair, so the recipe stays numeric and reproducible.
Screen images at 72–96 DPI placed small print acceptably; for a full-page map, generate at the largest size and highest scale factor offered, or print the interactive map from the browser.
